sources.file: (K) The Road Goes Ever On - A Song Cycle.pdf
sources.attribution: J.R.R. Tolkien, music Donald Swann (1967; 2nd ed. 1978)
sources.note: THE MOST WANTED OF THE ABSENT, because the archive ALREADY CITES IT: The War of the Jewels refers the reader to 'The Road Goes Ever On, p. 61' for miruvórë, so the corpus depends on a book it does not hold. Published in Tolkien's lifetime and carrying his own commentary on Namárië and A Elbereth Gilthoniel -- the only place he glossed those two texts word by word. ARRIVED 2026-07-30 AND IS AN IMAGE-ONLY SCAN, 78pp with no text layer. The dependency this row was written about is therefore NOT resolved: the corpus still cites 'The Road Goes Ever On, p. 61' for miruvórë and still cannot read the page. Held, and uncitable until OCR'd and checked. EXTRACTION: SILENTLY MISSING — the words are on the page and only the text layer is absent, which is the sharpest thing that can be said about §1 today: the most wanted volume in this register arrived, and the citation that wanted it still cannot be followed.

sources.file: secondary sources/A Secret Vice - Tolkien on Invented Languages.pdf
sources.attribution: J.R.R. Tolkien, ed. Dimitra Fimi & Andrew Higgins (2016)
sources.note: Tolkien's own essay on language invention with the associated manuscripts. Tier 1 as HIS WORDS about his own languages; the editors' apparatus is theirs and is cited as such where used. ARRIVED 2026-07-30 IN CLEAN TEXT, 180pp -- the 1931 lecture with the drafts and the essay on phonetic symbolism. AND THIS ROW CORRECTED ME: I had tiered it 2 for its editors, and the reason written here before the book came is the right one. It is the foundation document for what the languages hall says about WHY the languages exist, which the archive has until now had to infer.

Nothing cites this book, and it is film art rather than Middle-earth, so its absence costs no lore.

'Words of Joy: Five Catholic Prayers in Quenya' -- part one of two, printing Tolkien's own hitherto unpublished Quenya translations of the Pater Noster (Ataremma), the Ave Maria (Aia Maria) and the Gloria Patri (Alcar i Ataren), with the manuscript variants and the editors' analysis. The remaining two prayers -- Sub Tuum Praesidium and the Litany of Loreto -- are in VT 44, which is NOT held. The journal sits at tier 2 because it is published by the Estate's permission; the Quenya inside it is Tolkien's own and carries tier-1 authority, which is what primary_text records. The texts remain the Estate's: they may be read and cited, and are not the archive's to reproduce.

sources.attribution: Tolkien Gateway contributors, printed from the wiki 2026-07-25
sources.note: A 35-page print of the Tolkien Gateway's heraldry article. TIER 4 BY THE RULING OF 29 JULY, which settled this exact case in advance — that ruling defines t4 as a source carrying no independent authority, usable only where it happens to restate something Tolkien wrote, and says in the same breath that this is exactly what a wiki is. THE QUOTATION MARKS CAME OFF THAT SENTENCE DELIBERATELY: quoted_check reads any quoted span in a published dataset as a span owing verification against the corpus, and CLAUDE.md is not in the corpus. Quoting the archive's own ruling inside a register note grew the ratchet by one and the guard was right to refuse it — a rule of this archive is not a source for a claim about Arda. IT SAT AT THE REPOSITORY ROOT, UNSHELVED AND UNREGISTERED, SINCE 25 JULY, and surfaced only because the owner supplied his own list of what should be held and it was reconciled file by file against the shelf. Nothing else would have found it: every guard here checks the register against the corpus or the corpus against the register, and a book in NEITHER is invisible to all of them. The heraldry hall already holds the archive's own devices and Tolkien_heraldry.pdf at tier 3; this is consulted where it restates him and cited as a wiki where it does not.

not_held.title: The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien — Revised and Expanded Edition (2023), letters 43-354 and 40a onward
not_held.attribution: ed. Carpenter & C. Tolkien; revised Hammond & Scull
not_held.note: PARTLY HELD as of 2026-07-24. The excerpt now on the shelf gives the complete contents list — 508 letters, the 354 of 1981 plus 154 added — and the full text of letters 1 to 42, including thirteen that 1981 never printed. What is still missing is the text of the remaining 141 new letters, and the passages the revision restored to letters 43-354.
not_held.affects: The archive may now name which letters exist, to whom and when, for the whole edition. It may quote only 1-42 from the revision, and must otherwise cite the 1981 text. It still may not assert that a subject is absent from the Letters.

not_held.title: The Monsters and the Critics and Other Essays (1983)
not_held.note: Tolkien's scholarly essays, including 'On Fairy-Stories' and 'English and Welsh'. IT ALSO PRINTS 'A Secret Vice', AND THAT ESSAY IS NOW HELD SEPARATELY in the fuller Fimi & Higgins edition of 2016, with the drafts and the essay on phonetic symbolism that this collection does not carry. So what is still wanted here is 'On Fairy-Stories' and 'English and Welsh', not the Secret Vice.
not_held.affects: The languages hall, and any statement about Tolkien's philosophy of invention.

not_held.title: The Bovadium Fragments (2025)
not_held.attribution: ed. Christopher Tolkien; essay by Richard Ovenden
not_held.note: A previously unpublished satire on the motor-car and the ruin of Oxford, and the last of Christopher Tolkien's presentations of his father's work. No Middle-earth matter.
not_held.affects: Nothing in this archive. Registered for completeness of the tier-1 shelf.

not_held.title: The Fall of Arthur (2013); The Legend of Sigurd and Gudrún (2009); Beowulf: A Translation and Commentary (2014); The Story of Kullervo (2015); The Lay of Aotrou and Itroun (2016)

not_held.title: Roverandom; Mr Bliss; Letters from Father Christmas; Smith of Wootton Major

not_held.title: Parma Eldalamberon 12, 16, 18–22 (1995– )
not_held.attribution: ed. Elvish Linguistic Fellowship, by permission of the Tolkien Estate and with Christopher Tolkien's support
not_held.note: MOSTLY ANSWERED ON 2026-07-30, AND THIS ENTRY IS THE RECORD OF WHAT IT ASKED FOR. It used to name PE 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19 and 22 as the single largest body of primary Tolkien not held. Numbers 11, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 23 have since arrived and are registered above — so the Gnomish Lexicon, Early Noldorin and 'Words, Phrases and Passages' are on the shelf. STILL NOT HELD: the Qenya Lexicon (PE 12) and the Quenya phonology and verb structure (PE 16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22). Giraudeau's derived lexicons at tier 3 give partial access to 12 and 21 and are not a substitute for either. The distinction this entry drew before the volumes came is still the important one: the five issues that arrived on 2026-07-24 are Volume 1, numbers 1-5, the 1971-74 fanzine of the Mythopoeic Linguistic Fellowship containing no Tolkien manuscript, and they remain at tier 3. That is a different publication under the same name. The modern series' text is Tolkien's and carries tier-1 authority; the journals are the Estate-permitted vehicle.
not_held.affects: The languages hall above all. Its lexicon is built from the Etymologies (HoME V) and the published appendices; PE 17 and PE 22 would correct and greatly enlarge it. Until these are read, no entry in that hall should be presented as the whole of what Tolkien wrote.

not_held.title: Vinyar Tengwar — the issues outside 11–14, 24–25, 27–31, 36–39 and 41–50
not_held.attribution: ed. Elvish Linguistic Fellowship, by Estate permission
not_held.note: LARGELY ANSWERED ON 2026-07-30. This entry asked for 'Ósanwe-kenta', 'Notes on Óre', 'The Rivers and Beacon-hills of Gondor' and the Quenya prayers, and all four are now held: nos. 41-50 arrived as one 404-page volume of clean text, and Ósanwe-kenta as a clean extract of no. 39. WHAT IS HELD IS NOT THE SAME AS WHAT IS READABLE, and for this run the gap is wide: of the twenty-two issues now on the shelf, ELEVEN ARE IMAGE-ONLY SCANS and TWO MORE carry OCR so corrupt it must not be extracted. Readable today: nos. 41-50, no. 43, and the Ósanwe-kenta extract. Still not held at all: the issues below 11, and 15-23, 26, 30, 32-35, 38, 40.
not_held.affects: The languages hall; also the cosmology and any statement about Elvish mind and spirit.

not_held.title: The Art of The Lord of the Rings (2015)
not_held.note: Tolkien's own drawings, maps and designs for The Lord of the Rings, reproduced in full. ITS COMPANION, The Art of The Hobbit, ARRIVED 2026-07-30 and is registered above — as an image-only scan, so its captions are held and not yet readable either.
not_held.affects: The gallery and the maps. His own cartography outranks any reconstruction the archive draws. Wanted for the captions and datings; under the artwork ruling the plates are not republished.

not_held.title: Tolkien: Maker of Middle-earth (2018)
not_held.note: The exhibition catalogue: manuscripts, letters and artwork, including heraldic devices.

not_held.title: The Hobbit: Graphic Novel — new edition (September 2026)
not_held.attribution: adapted by Chuck Dixon and Sean Deming; illustrated by David Wenzel; first published 1989-90
not_held.note: An authorised adaptation, not a source. Its text is Tolkien's story abridged into panels and its pictures are Wenzel's reading of it, so nothing in it can settle a question of fact: where it differs from The Hobbit, The Hobbit wins. Tiered 3 by the user's judgement on 2026-07-24 — licensed by the Estate, which would argue for tier 2, but the tier records what a source IS, and an adaptation stands beside Fonstad's atlas rather than beside a published text.
not_held.affects: Nothing in this archive rests on it, and nothing should. Of interest only to the gallery, as one more record of how the tale has been visualised — and there it would be cited as Wenzel's art, never as evidence for how anything in Middle-earth looked.

derived.attribution: transcribed by this archive from The Lord of the Rings, Appendices A III, C and E
derived.note: Those tables are printed as images and survive no text extraction. They were recovered by rendering each plate with pdftoppm and reading it. OCR was tried and rejected: tesseract read Nain I's date as 1882 where the plate says 1832. Treat every figure here as a transcription that can be checked against the plate, not as extracted text.

rule: Where two sources disagree, the lower tier number wins. A tier-5 file is corrected by any tier above it. Tolkien's own words quoted inside a tier-2 book carry tier-1 authority; the editor's framing does not.

limits.what: The genealogical tables of Appendix A III (Durin's Folk) and Appendix C (the hobbit trees)
limits.why: In the edition held here these tables are embedded as IMAGES, not text, so no text extraction reaches them. They have now been recovered by rendering the pages and reading the plates directly, and cross-checked with tesseract OCR.
limits.effect: RESOLVED. The Dwarf line is verified against App A III: six birth-years were wrong in this archive and are corrected (Nain I was out by 101 years). The hobbit dates are verified against App C and were correct in every case checked, but now carry the warrant they lacked. Where OCR and a direct reading disagreed, the reading was confirmed at 450 dpi and OCR was found to be the one in error.
